notes: Summary: mid-market adtech DSP building sub-50ms tail latency scoring for auction-time reranking and personalization.
Primary pain: current stack (in-house endpoints) hits 120-250ms tail under burst; cost per decision is high due to small batch sizes and no KV caching.
Quote from CTO on intro call: "If tail latency spikes, we lose auctions — 100ms headroom is non-negotiable."
Interest areas: dynamic batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated user context, int8/4-bit quantization to reduce GPU footprint, model fallback routing to cheaper small models on load.
Perf targets discussed: p50 < 15ms, p95 < 50ms, sustainable 5k qps for scoring with 1-2s request windows for some cohorts.
Cost goal: reduce per-decision token cost by ~60% vs current hosted baseline; evaluate Dedicated reserved pool economics vs hosted API bursts.
Security asks: full SOC2/AICPA evidence, KMS integration for model and inference keys, audit logs shipped to customer SIEM, option for VPC peering.
POC constraints: must run in NA region only; no external logs of raw request payloads outside VPC; retention TTL limits for cached prefixes.
Stakeholders: CTO (Ravi Patel) sponsor; Head of ML (Maya Lopez) owns model tests; Infra lead (Gabe Turner) owns network/VPC; Procurement lead (S. Walker) on contract terms.
Competitive notes: evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted APIs; key differentiator is desire for predictable reserved throughput + fine-grained batching/quantization controls.
Internal note: SE call 2026-02-10 went deep on batching knobs — they want recommended bin sizes by latency SLO and a sample kernel profile report.
Follow-ups: share perf-benchmark template, run baseline trace using their test harness (JMeter script), schedule 48h dedicated POC for early March.

requirements_summary: Workload: auction-time reranking + personalization scoring; mix of short-context prompts (<=64 tokens) and user-history embeddings.
Latency/throughput: p95 < 50ms, sustain 5k qps with <10ms per-request overhead for routing layer.
Cost sensitivity: high — prefers reserved capacity if unit cost reduction >40%, otherwise aggressive batching/quantization to achieve targets.
Model prefs: can deploy open LLM variants; want smaller distilled candidates for fallback; need model version pinning and rollout controls.
Routing/fallback: smart routing by latency SLA and cost tier; automatic fallback to quantized model when under heavy load.
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and traces linked to internal request IDs.
Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts + TTL controls; cache must be optional per-route and auditable.
Benchmarking asks: provide Redwood perf report (kernel selection, batch size vs latency curves), and reproducible harness for their infra.
Compliance: VPC peering, KMS integrations, audit log delivery to SIEM; data residency: US only.
